AlternateTargets: the five ranks of ruler and minister
Senses.Explanation: The technical name of the Caodong house's signature scheme, created by Dongshan Liangjie and systematized by Caoshan Benji. 'Five' configurations arrange two terms — the upright or straight (正) and the crooked or bent (偏) — as: crooked within the upright (正中偏), upright within the crooked (偏中正), coming from within the upright (正中來), arriving from both together (兼中至 / 偏中至), attained in both together (兼中到). The same five are recast as ruler and minister (君臣, the 君臣五位); Dongshan also taught parallel fivefold sets — the five ranks of merit/achievement (功勳五位) and the five ranks of princes (王子五位) — and Caoshan's 'five ranks facing the guest' (五位對賓) works them into interview form ('I come from the crooked position, please receive me into the upright'). Across the corpus the term functions as the emblem of the Caodong house, almost always named in one breath with its Linji-house counterpart, the three mysteries (and three essentials) (臨濟三玄（三要）) — 'Dongshan's five ranks / Linji's three mysteries' (洞山五位／臨濟三玄), 'not Linji's three mysteries, not Caodong's five ranks' (不是臨濟三玄不是曹洞五位) — so that 'the Five Ranks' effectively names the Caodong house the way 'three mysteries' names the Linji house. The scheme is defined inside the house's own records. Dongshan composed the verses: 'Dongshan composed the verses on the five ranks of ruler and minister: Crooked within the upright — the third watch, early in the night, before the moon shines; no wonder that meeting they do not recognize each other, dimly still harboring the old days' estrangement' (師。作五位君臣頌云。正中偏。三更初夜月明前。莫怪相逢不相識。隱隱猶懷舊日嫌, T47n1986B). Caoshan, asked for the essential formula of ruler and minister (君臣旨訣), lays the terms out: 'the upright position is the realm of emptiness — originally not a thing; the crooked position is the realm of form — having the shapes of the myriad images; crooked-within-upright: turning from principle toward affairs; upright-within-crooked: leaving affairs and entering principle; both-together: darkly answering the many conditions without falling into any existent' (正位即空界。本來無物。偏位即色界。有萬象形。正中偏者背理就事。偏中正者舍事入理。兼帶者冥應眾緣。不墮諸有) and 'ruler = the upright position, minister = the crooked position; minister facing ruler is upright-within-crooked, ruler regarding minister is crooked-within-upright, ruler and minister's ways joined is the both-together saying' (君為正位。臣為偏位。臣向君是偏中正。君視臣是正中偏。君臣道合是兼帶語) (T47n1987A, the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Caoshan Yuanzheng of Fuzhou; the 'ruler = the upright position' (君為正位) mapping recurs 11 times, including T47n1987B and the Eyes of Humans and Gods, T48n2006). The Eyes of Humans and Gods also glosses each fivefold set: 'the five ranks of merit clarify the stages of effort in study, up to the stage beyond effort; the five ranks of ruler and minister clarify the conditioned and the unconditioned; the five ranks of princes clarify that inward succession is originally complete of itself, while outward succession has an end and a beginning; roughly, the Caodong house style is nothing beyond substance/function, upright/crooked, host/guest, to clarify the road going beyond' (功勳五位者。明參學功位至於非功位也。君臣五位者。明有為無為也。王子五位者。明內紹本自圓成。外紹有終有始也。大約曹洞家風。不過體用偏正賓主。以明向上一路) — and the ranks in substance/function terms: 'crooked-within-upright: substance giving rise to function; upright-within-crooked: function returning to substance; arriving-from-both: substance and function arriving together; attained-in-both: substance and function both extinguished' (正中偏者。體起用也。偏中正者。用歸體也。兼中至。體用並至也。兼中到。體用俱泯也) (T48n2006). Like other stock house vocabulary, it is asked as an interview question: asked 'What are the five ranks of the Dong[shan] school?' (如何是洞上五位), Sanyi Mingyu answers 'old door-gods on New Year's Eve' (除夜舊門神) (問：「如何是洞上五位？」荅：「除夜舊門神。」, J27nB189).
Senses.Note: Attribution (not disputed, but a division of labour): the upright-crooked (正偏) Five Ranks are Dongshan Liangjie's; the ruler-minister (君臣) formulation and the 'facing the guest' (五位對賓) catechism are especially Caoshan Benji's. Witness J10nA158 is a LINJI master reciting the four fivefold schemata (ruler-minister 君臣, upright-crooked 偏正, princes 王子, merit 功勳) precisely to contrast them with Linji's own 'true person of no rank' (無位真人) — an outside witness that still fixes the term's meaning. SenseKey is null because the scheme becomes shared Caodong-house vocabulary; Dongshan's historical origin does not make the later meaning private to him. Zen-allowlist grep counts: the Five Ranks (五位), 1,155 hits in 212 of 462 texts. Rank names: crooked within the upright (正中偏) 315, upright within the crooked (偏中正) 296, attained in both (兼中到) 270, coming from within the upright (正中來) 269; for the fourth rank both 'arriving from both' (兼中至, 192) and 'arriving from the crooked' (偏中至, 86) are attested. Emblems and set names: ruler-and-minister (五位君臣 188 / 君臣五位 46), Dongshan's five ranks (洞山五位) 111, Caodong five ranks (曹洞五位) 30, the Dong-school five ranks (洞上五位) 13, princes (五位王子 41 / 王子五位 11), merit (功勳五位 20 / 五位功勳 17), facing the guest (五位對賓) 16 (variant graph 對賔 1).

Occurrences.Kwic: 示以偏正五位。四賓主功勳五位。君臣五位。王子五位。內外紹等事。偏正五位者。正中偏者。體起用也。偏中正者。用歸體也。兼中至。體用並至也。兼中到。體用俱泯也。四賓主。不同臨濟。主中賓。體中用也。賓中主。用中體也。賓中賓。用中用。頭上安頭也。主中主。物我雙忘。人法俱泯。不涉正偏位也。功勳五位者。明參學功位至於非功位也。君臣五位者。明有為無為也。王子五位者。明內紹本自圓成。外紹有終有始也。大約曹洞家風。不過體用偏正賓主。以明向上一路。

Senses.Explanation: The ordinary Chinese reading — 'five positions/ranks/stages' — used non-technically even inside Zen texts: as a plain ordinal ('who is the fifth-ranked sage?'), or as the path-positions of the scholastic literature ('lodged in the five causal positions' 寄因五位, the provisional positions up to the fruit-position; also embedded in 五十五位, the fifty-five bodhisattva stages). Distinguished from the Caodong technical sense purely by context: no pairing with upright and crooked or ruler and minister, no link to Dongshan or Caoshan, and no coupling with Linji's three mysteries. Recorded only so the 'Five Ranks' reading is not projected onto every place these two graphs occur.
Senses.Note: Peripheral and heterogeneous (an ordinal in one witness, scholastic path-stages in the other); the two share only 'NOT the Caodong term.' Kept minimal, for disambiguation. Provisional because it is not a single unified Zen sense so much as the residue of the plain Chinese word. Other generic uses inside the allowlist, with grep counts: the fifty-five bodhisattva stages (五十五位) 9, the hundred things in five groups (五位百法) 3, and the five stages in the womb (在胎五位) 1 in the Record of the Source-Mirror, T48n2016.
